newsitem.title: INDIA: India cotton prices steady, rising export demand.
newsitem.headline: India cotton prices steady, rising export demand.

text.p: Indian cotton prices firmed on Monday, fuelled by rising expoort demand and slowing arrivals, dealers said.
Fresh mill buying remained slow but limited arrivals and shortage of ready stock dragged prices upward on the back of speculative support.
"Sentiment remained firm on reports of falling arrivals in producing centres as the season drew to a close, and on higher export demand for Indian cotton yarn," one broker said.
"Higher overseas demand for cotton yarn may prompt fresh buying for raw cotton by the spinning mills," he said.
Daily arrivals of cotton in the Punjab region dropped to 1,000/1,500 bales (170 kg each).

Meanwhile in the spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 10 rupees to 910/940 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned rose by 25 rupees at 1,650/1,700 rupees per maund. F-414 rose to 1,955/1,970 rupees per maund from 1,930/1,945 rupees. Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) rose by 300 rupees to 13,900/14,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
